findings.title: Legacy API route authentication and authorization are not demonstrated
findings.surface: All 36 FastAPI routes; especially mutative and provider-capable routes
evidence: No Depends/Security/OAuth/JWT/Bearer route dependency found in scoped static search
findings.impact: If the app is exposed without an external edge control, read and mutation surfaces lack demonstrated identity, owner, tenant or resource authorization.
findings.condition: Requires actual app exposure or a hosting edge policy not present in current repo evidence.

findings.title: Global CORS wildcard remains on the FastAPI app
findings.surface: All routes registered on the app
findings.impact: Cross-origin exposure is broad at source level; credentials and deployment overrides were not demonstrated.
findings.condition: Applies if this app is served in the assessed deployment without a narrower edge/middleware override.

findings.title: POST /api/settings is secret-bearing and writes settings/config paths
findings.impact: A supplied key can enter handler memory, settings persistence and config rewrite; source does not demonstrate route auth or redaction before response construction.
findings.condition: Requires a real request supplying a key and a reachable writable deployment.

findings.title: POST /api/chat is a legacy provider-capable orchestration path
findings.impact: The route can be source-callable into provider/network-capable adapters and memory/orchestration side effects; dedicated runtime gate coverage is not demonstrated.
findings.condition: Requires Supervisor startup, provider/config availability and actual request execution.

findings.title: Multiple legacy mutation routes expose write candidates without demonstrated route authz
findings.impact: Source-level file, memory, evolution and agent mutation candidates are present; ownership and permission boundaries are not demonstrated locally.
findings.condition: Requires route exposure and handler execution.

findings.title: Dedicated runtime/execution/confirmation contracts are disabled but not proven global over legacy API
findings.surface: runtime_activation_gate, attempt_factory, active_executor, confirmation gate versus legacy API
findings.impact: The contract plane provides important negative controls, but their global coverage of old route chains remains an explicit unknown.
findings.condition: Requires a complete call graph or runtime tracing, both outside this read-only mission.

findings.title: Provider and network reachability cannot be closed statically
findings.surface: NVIDIA requests adapter, Ollama urllib adapter, registry health/preload paths
findings.impact: Static source confirms network-capable adapters, not actual network reachability or deployment invocation.
findings.condition: Requires external/runtime evidence prohibited by this mission.

negative_evidence_limits: Static absence of route auth dependency does not prove absence of hosting-edge auth.
A source-callable provider path does not prove runtime or deployment reachability.
A source write candidate does not prove a real request reached the write or that a file was changed.
Disabled dedicated flags do not prove every legacy path traverses those gates.
No route invocation means no positive/negative behavior claim about actual HTTP responses.
